text:
incident-bot: P1 alert — eu-west-1 node(s) reporting ephemeralDiskPressure -> multiple model-server pods evicted and restart loop. Auto-pager to SRE rotation.

kubebot: kubelet eviction summary for node gpu-eu-12: Eviction signal: nodefs.available, reclaimable: 0%, reason: PodOOM or filesystem pressure. Pods evicted: modelcache-1, runtime-a-5, runtime-b-9.

sara-oncall: ack. I'm on it, joining. seeing repeated OOMKilled on runtime containers after eviction, then CUDA init failures on restart.

mike-eng-runtime: adding logs from runtime on one crashed pod: ```
[2026-03-15T02:11:43Z] INFO modelcache: loading shard 3 -> /var/lib/modelcache/shard-3 mmap failed: ENOSPC
[2026-03-15T02:11:44Z] ERROR runtime: failed to allocate kv cache 256MB -> OOMKilled
[2026-03-15T02:11:45Z] FATAL runtime: cuda: failed to init device 0: CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS
ContainerStatus: State: Terminated (OOMKilled)
```

hana-sre: confirmed node root fs at 99% used. Large logfile growth from modelcache checkpointing + debug level logs from a churned pod. Also saw heavy write amplification to /var/scratch by backup job.

sara-oncall: immediate mitigation steps: 1) mark node unschedulable (cordon) 2) drain non-critical pods 3) move modelcache shards off node 4) scale down runtime replicas to prevent churn 5) notify CS for potential customer impact. I'll run cordon now.

sara-oncall: `/usr/bin/kubectl cordon gpu-eu-12 && /usr/bin/kubectl drain gpu-eu-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --force --grace-period=30`

kubebot: drain started. Evicting 12 pods, 3 of which have emptyDir. Notified kube-controller to relocate modelcache pv claims.

mike-eng-runtime: while cordon is running, suggest reducing modelcache checkpoint frequency and disabling debug logging on shard owners to stop write spikes. Patch ready: set env MODELCACHE_CHECKPOINT_INTERVAL=300s -> 1200s, LOG_LEVEL=info. ETA to rollout config: ~4 minutes.

hana-sre: node fs cleanup in progress. Found runaway logs at `/var/lib/modelcache/shard-3/checkpoint.log` (~28GB) from a misbehaving checkpoint loop. Truncating and rotating now. Command: `sudo truncate -s 0 /var/lib/modelcache/shard-3/checkpoint.log`

mike-eng-runtime: deploying hotfix config to modelcache owners in eu-west-1: rolling restart 6 pods (rate 2/s). Applying config via kustomize.

ryan-cs: ping — CS: we have 2 customers on dedicated instances in eu-west-1 showing increased 5xxs and elevated latencies ~2x. No data loss reported, some requests timed out. Messaging customers now.

emily-support: creating incident notification to customers: short note with mitigation and ETA for stabilizing (target 30min). Will include guidance to retry and fallback to hosted if they need immediate recovery.

incident-bot: Incident status update: evictions in progress; degraded API error rate 4.8% -> baseline 0.1%. Severity remains P1.

sara-oncall: after truncating logs and cordon, node frees ~32GB, kubelet stops evicting. However some runtime processes still crash on restart with CUDA illegal address — likely due to corrupted GPU driver state after OOM. Plan: full restart of affected GPU node once workloads drained.

hana-sre: scheduling reboot: `sudo systemctl reboot` on gpu-eu-12 in 2m after final pods drained. We'll move modelcache PVs to other nodes first.

mike-eng-runtime: to reduce risk of repeated GPU init failures, will push runtime change to initialize CUDA device with retry/backoff and NVML reset protection. Patch note: catch CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS -> sleep 5s -> retry init x3; if still failing, fallback to CPU-only worker and mark instance degraded. Deploying hotfix to runtime controller group.

sara-oncall: handover note for next oncall: current node cordoned and rebooting, modelcache shards redistributed, runtime replica count temporarily halved to reduce churn. API error rate dropped to 1.3% after mitigation, but some 5xx persist while rebalances finish. My pager is still active until stable.

mike-eng-runtime: logs show one pod that lost persistent metadata causing modelcache to re-download weight slices and blow disk; added guard to check free space before starting heavy checkpoint. Code snippet going out in PR: ```bash
if [ $(df --output=avail /var/lib/modelcache | tail -n1) -lt $((1024*1024)) ]; then
  echo "insufficient space for checkpoint, delaying"
  exit 1
fi
```

emily-support: updated customers: initial note sent, calm responses; one customer asked for timeline for completed repair, provided 30-45min.

ryan-cs: logged internal customer impact: 2 dedicated customers with elevated errors, default hosted customers saw minor latency blips under 3%. Escalation to account execs not required yet but we'll follow up.

hana-sre: post-mitigation checks: node reboot completed, kubelet healthy, modelcache pods stabilized. Free space on node now 42GB. No further evictions in last 12 minutes.

sara-oncall: closing active paging window in 15m if metrics remain stable. Action items for postmortem:
- root cause analysis: why checkpoint loop didn't check free space
- add disk pressure alert with earlier threshold (currently too late)
- require modelcache to truncate old logs/rotate aggressively
- runtime: add cuda init retry and CPU fallback path
- ops: ensure backup jobs write to dedicated PV not node root

mike-eng-runtime: I'll own the runtime PR and the init-fallback. Target merge + canary tomorrow.

emily-support: will follow up with customers with a postmortem summary and any credits if SLA breached.

sara-oncall: final summary for thread: immediate cause was ephemeral disk saturation from modelcache checkpoint log growth + backup job writing to local scratch, leading to kubelet nodefs eviction and subsequent runtime OOM/CUDA init failures on restart. Mitigations applied: cordon/drain, truncate logs, scale down replicas, hotfix config to checkpoint frequency, reboot node. Impact: brief increase in 5xxs for a small set of customers; stabilized within ~45 minutes. Handoff complete.

incident-bot: Incident P1 -> Mitigated. Postmortem requested.
